results.text:
2026 · Mariana F. Nery, Lucas Albuquerque, Beatriz Daros · BMC Biology · Journal Article
TL;DR: This study presents the first chromosome-level genome assembly of the Guiana dolphin and the first genome sequence of the riverine tucuxi, revealing their divergence during Plio-Pleistocene sea-level fluctuations and highlighting conservation concerns due to low genetic diversity.
Abstract: The transition from terrestrial to aquatic life is well documented in cetaceans, yet secondary transitions between marine and freshwater habitats remain poorly understood. The dolphin genus Sotalia provides an exceptional natural system for investigating this process, comprising two recently diverged species (~ 2 Ma) that occupy contrasting environments: the coastal Guiana dolphin ( Sotalia guianensis ) and the riverine tucuxi ( Sotalia fluviatilis ). results.title: Fishers’ knowledge as a source of information about the estuarine dolphin (Sotalia guianensis, van Bénéden, 1864)
results.text:
2015 · Maíra Fontes Manzan, Priscila F. M. Lopes · Environmental Monitoring and Assessment · Journal Article
TL;DR: It is shown that the type of environment most used by fishers also affects the accuracy of the information they provide, and when designing studies to gather information on species and/or populations, special consideration should be given to local particularities such as gear and habitats used within the fishing community.
Abstract: Fishers’ local ecological knowledge (LEK) is an additional tool to obtain information about cetaceans, regarding their local particularities, fishing interactions, and behavior. However, this knowledge could vary in depth of detail according to the level of interaction that fishers have with a specific species. results.title: Habitat use of Guiana dolphin (Sotalia guianensis) in a heavily urbanized embayment
results.text:
Aco de Meirelles, KF Choi-Lima, TM Campos Vila Nova · Marine Ecology Progress Series · Journal Article
TL;DR: This study applied generalized additive models to identify Guiana dolphin habitat use in a heavily urbanized embayment, revealing preferences for areas with less complex seabed, near breakwaters and fishing grounds, driven by foraging opportunities and "barrier-feeding" strategies.
Abstract: Understanding environmental and anthropogenic variables that influence the presence of dolphins in coastal areas is fundamental for conservation planning and forecasting. In this study, we applied generalized additive models to identify areas of high probability of occurrence of Guiana dolphins in Mucuripe embayment, a heavily urbanized area in northeastern Brazil. Sighting and effort data were collected during systematic, boat-based surveys between 2009 and 2011. results.title: Risk areas for marine mammals in Colombia
results.text:
Isabel Cristina Avila, Alan Giraldo
TL;DR: Marine mammals in Colombia face diverse threats, including bycatch, direct capture, vessel traffic, and habitat alteration, with 22 species affected, and 10 high-risk areas identified, necessitating urgent evaluation and management actions.
Abstract: Introduction: Marine mammals are affected by diverse threats that must be identified for mitigation efforts. Objective: To visually quantify threats to marine mammals in Colombia, and to identify mitigation actions. Methods: We georeferenced threats based on the literature, covering 35 species in the period 1991-2020, and superimposed them on species range maps. Results: 22 species had at least one threat. TL;DR: This study examines the site-fidelity of Guiana dolphins in a protected marine area in Northeastern Brazil, finding that while most individuals are occasional visitors, some are regular and highly faithful to the area, with implications for conservation strategies.
